chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', who said:

I heard al-Rida عليه السلام saying: When the sun passes the meridian while you are in the town and you intend to travel, then perform it in full; but when you depart after noon, then shorten the 'Asr prayer.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, indicating the onset of zuhr time
key_terms.الْمِصْرِ: the town or place of residence
key_terms.زَالَتِ: passed the meridian; the beginning of noon time
key_terms.فَقَصِّرِ: shorten the prayer as a traveler

ai.seo_question: How should a traveler pray if the prayer time begins before leaving town?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about prayer for one who is still resident when the time enters but intends to travel. It indicates that if noon begins while he is still in the town, he performs the prayer in full, and after departing he shortens the 'Asr prayer.
